title: Unpointed Picard sheaf representability for proper flat algebraic spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $f:X\to S$ a proper flat finitely presented morphism from an algebraic space [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Proper means separated, of finite type and universally closed; flatness and local finite presentation are tested on etale scheme charts, and finite presentation also includes quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness. A geometric fibre is a base change to the spectrum of an algebraically closed field; integral means nonempty, reduced and irreducible. A line module means a module on the small etale structure sheaf locally isomorphic to that structure sheaf [def-trf-algebraic-space]; on a scheme it corresponds to an ordinary invertible module [def-sc-invertible-module]. For every $S$-scheme $T$, put $X_T=X\times_ST$, and let $\operatorname{Pic}(X_T)$ be the group of line-module isomorphism classes under tensor product. Let $F$ be the fppf sheafification of the presheaf $T\mapsto\operatorname{Pic}(X_T)$ on the big fppf site [def-pc-fppf-site]. Suppose $\mathcal O_T\to(f_T)_*\mathcal O_{X_T}$ is an isomorphism for every $S$-scheme $T$. Then $F$ is represented by an algebraic space $Q\to S$ which is quasi-separated and locally of finite presentation. Quasi-separated means that the diagonal is quasi-compact; local finite presentation is tested on etale scheme charts. The tensor product, trivial module and dual module induce a commutative group algebraic space structure on $Q$. No section, geometric integrality, dimension or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed. Direct image and tensor pullback are the canonical functors on small etale module sheaves [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors].

proof.text: Let $\mathcal P(T)$ be the groupoid of line modules on $X_T$ and tensor-pullback isomorphisms. Apply [lem-sfb-space-coherent-stack-general] with $B=S$: properness gives separatedness, and $f$ is finitely presented. Its coherent stack $\mathcal C$ is algebraic and locally of finite presentation over $S$. By [lem-sfb-space-invertible-open-coherent], $\mathcal P\to\mathcal C$ is fully faithful and representable by open immersions; flatness and properness of $f$ are exactly its hypotheses. Consequently [lem-sfb-open-stack-algebraic-lfp] makes $\mathcal P$ algebraic and locally of finite presentation over $S$. In particular every line module used below is an object of this coherent stack, with the finite-presentation, relative-flatness and proper-support conditions stated there.

For a line module $L$ on $X_T$, an automorphism is multiplication by a unique global unit: in a local frame it is a unit scalar, and change of frame does not change that scalar. The hypothesis $\mathcal O_T\simeq(f_T)_*\mathcal O_{X_T}$ therefore gives $\operatorname{Aut}(L)=\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)^\times$, naturally after every further scheme base change. The inertia projection of $\mathcal P$ thus pulls back at $L$ to $\mathbf G_{m,T}\to T$. Over an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq T$, this unit functor is represented by $\operatorname{Spec}(A[z,w]/(zw-1))$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], a finitely presented affine scheme [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. It is formally smooth: for any square-zero ring surjection $R'\twoheadrightarrow R$, lift a unit and its inverse to $a,b\in R'$. If $ab=1+i$ with $i^2=0$, then $b(1-i)$ is an inverse of $a$, giving the required lift. By [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] this scheme is smooth. Locality on the open affine cover and smooth-implies-flat-and-locally-finitely-presented in [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus] imply that the inertia is flat and locally of finite presentation.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-flat-inertia-algebraic-space-quotient], the fppf sheafification of $T\mapsto\operatorname{Ob}\mathcal P(T)/\cong$ is an algebraic space $Q$. This presheaf is exactly $T\mapsto\operatorname{Pic}(X_T)$, so the sheaf is the $F$ of the statement. There has been no choice of a section of $f$. Work in a containing universe as in [def-pc-fppf-site]. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local], sections of $F$ have local line-module representatives, and two representatives with equal images become isomorphic on a further fppf covering. Thus $\pi:\mathcal P\to Q$ is a gerbe: over every scheme mapping to $Q$, its fibre has objects locally and any two objects are locally isomorphic.

proof.text: Choose a smooth surjective scheme atlas $U\to\mathcal P$ with $U\to S$ locally of finite presentation, available from step 1. The gerbe assertion of step 3 and [lem-sfb-gerbe-smooth-universal-homeomorphism] make the composite $U\to Q$ surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation. Apply the source-locality clause of [lem-sfb-representable-fppf-etale-open-descent] to the space morphism $Q\to S$, using the identity cover $V=S\to S$ and the source cover $W=U\to Q$. Since $U\to S$ is locally of finite presentation, $Q\to S$ is locally of finite presentation. This applies locality to morphisms of algebraic spaces, not to the nonrepresentable gerbe projection.

proof.text: For every $S$-scheme $T$ and pair $L,M\in\mathcal P(T)$, the projection $f_T:X_T\to T$ is of finite presentation by [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality]. Step 1 supplies finite presentation, relative flatness and proper support for both modules. Apply [lem-sfb-space-module-isom-affine] to $f_T,L,M$. It represents their isomorphism functor by an algebraic space affine and of finite presentation over $T$. This functor is precisely the pullback of $\Delta_{\mathcal P/S}$ by the object $(L,M)$ over $T$, by the definition of the two-fibre product. Hence that diagonal is of finite presentation and in particular quasi-compact. Apply [lem-sfb-gerbe-qc-diagonal-descent] to the gerbe of step 3. It gives quasi-compactness of $\Delta_{Q/S}$, which is exactly the asserted quasi-separatedness of $Q\to S$.

Tensor product, the trivial module, and dualization give each $\operatorname{Pic}(X_T)$ its abelian group law and commute with tensor pullback. For $a,b\in F(T)$ choose a common fppf covering with representatives $L_i,M_i$, using [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local], and glue the images of $[L_i\otimes M_i]$. On overlaps equality of input classes is, locally, an isomorphism of the inputs, so these tensor-product classes have equal images in $F$; the sheaf condition gives a unique glued section. The same argument defines inverse by $L_i^\vee$ and identity by $\mathcal O_{X_T}$, and proves independence of representatives and compatibility with restriction. Associativity, commutativity, identity and inverse equations hold on representatives and therefore in $F$. Since morphisms of algebraic spaces are natural transformations of the representing sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space], and $Q\times_SQ$ is the sheaf fibre product, which represents $F\times F$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], these operations are morphisms $Q\times_SQ\to Q$, $S\to Q$ and $Q\to Q$ satisfying the group identities. This is the claimed commutative group algebraic space.
